newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- JAN 31.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- JAN 31.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:
KATHIMERINI

--Latest figures from the National Statistics Service indicate that inflation for January may fall to the unheard of levels of 6.9 percent, for the first time in decades. The news bodes well for the government achieving its target of 5.0 percent by the end of the year.

--The new uniform wage scale for public servants was submitted to Parliament last night with a number of adjustments to conditions for bonuses but no essential changes to wage levels. Unions, however, remain unsatisfied and will procced with the 48-hour strike next week.
--The development ministry considers latest increases on car insurance premiums - ranging from 15 percent for state-controlled insurance firms to 30 percent for private firms - low.
--The government will finally abolish a pension fund set up by the 1967-1974 military junta to provide pensions and benefits to unionists appointed by them to posts.
IMERISIA

--The government is determined to bring changes to the operation of the Athens Stock Exchange: National Economy and Finance Minister Yannos Papandoniou has decided to institute source of wealth statements for all ASE officials and brokers; to disallow any ASE president, member of the board or Capital Market Commission to be a "player"; and the ASE's participation, as well as that of institutional investors and private individuals in ASE's share capital.
--The National Mortgage and National Housing Banks will merge within 1997, with procedures discussed at yesterday's meeting of the boards of the two banks and the National Bank.
--Prime Minister Costas Simitis is calling a Cabinet meeting on the need to urge a speedier absorption of EU funds.
KERDOS

--Contained increases in the prices of goods and stringent checks and interventions in cases of abuse have aided in the battle against anti-inflationary pressures, Development Minister Vasso Papandreou said yesterday.
--The Greek state is called on to pay 48 billion drachmas in fines on 65 Greek transport companies found guilty of importing contraband cigarettes to Belgium and Holland.
--Farmers yesterday blocked rail lines in Larissa for one hour on the second day of what is developing into low-key protests.

--The rise of the dollar is expected to have positive repercussions on tourism in Europe, with the Greek National Tourism Organisation (GNTO) US director estimating a 20 poercent increase in US tourists this year.
EXPRESS
--The course of prices is favourable for 1997, Vasso Papandreou says, adding that inflation will fall with the growth of competition and not administrative measures.
NAFTEMBORIKI

--What the legalisation of foreigners and illegal immigrants means for the Greek labour market. New measures to combat illegal immigration foresee work permits for all, but without direct medical cover.
--The Agricultural Bank will sell off or close 30 subsidiary companies as part of the five-year plan to modernise and streamline. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
